DSM_neurodevelopmental.prop: SPECIAL-ED CLASSROOM — a brightly-colored kindergarten room with 6 distinct corners, each showing a child characteristic of one ND disorder family. ASD CORNER: child sits cross-legged silently lining up toy trains in a perfectly straight row, wears large noise-cancelling headphones, eyes averted. ADHD CORNER: child bouncing on a chair surrounded by scattered toys, motion-lines and 'POW!' 'WHIZ!' speech bubbles, multiple half-finished activities. INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY (IDD) CORNER: child works slowly on a 5-piece beginner puzzle with a patient teacher's helping hand visible behind. SPECIFIC LEARNING DISORDER (SLD) CORNER: child looks confused at letters that visually swap and float ('b/d/p/q' rotating chaotically), placards mixing up reading order. COMMUNICATION DISORDER CORNER: child with sealed lips and an empty speech bubble OR with the speech bubble shown broken into stuttering fragments. TIC DISORDERS CORNER: child surrounded by comic-style action bubbles popping around their head — 'BLINK!' 'SHRUG!' 'AH!' 'TWITCH!'. At the center of the classroom: a teacher pointing at a tree-branch chart titled 'Neurodevelopmental Disorders' with 6 branches.
DSM_neurodevelopmental.hook: Each corner = a specific ND disorder family with its hallmark visual. Same children reappear individually as the symbol
DSM_neurodevelopmental.category: Neurodevelopmental Disorders — establishing scene (Special-Ed Classroom) — 6 ND families

adhd.prop: ADHD's WHIRLWIND CLASSROOM — a child literally floats a few inches above their chair (hyperactive), legs in mid-kick, hair flying. Their desk is total chaos: pencils, papers, half-finished projects, dropped erasers, three different books open at once. THREE separate speech bubbles burst from their mouth simultaneously: 'Hey! Did you see — wait, what was I — OH! Look! — sorry — what?'. A clock shows they've changed activities 12 TIMES in one hour. Comic action-bubbles 'POW!' 'WHIZ!' 'ZIP!' surround them. A trail of dropped items winds across the floor behind them. A backpack hangs upside-down with contents spilling. The teacher in background looks exhausted, holding their head. BUT — importantly — the child is also handing a flower to another child while spinning (warmth/impulsivity, often misunderstood as 'bad'). Two scenes embedded: (a) at school + (b) at home — same chaos, demonstrating 'symptoms in 2+ settings'. A calendar showing the child has had these symptoms since age 5 (before age 12 cutoff).

communication_disorders.prop: SPEECH THERAPY ROOM — a colorful pediatric speech-therapy room with 4 vignettes showing the 4 communication disorder subtypes. CHILD 1 — LANGUAGE DISORDER: child at a table, struggling to find words; a thought bubble shows pictures of common objects (dog, cup, ball) but the SPEECH BUBBLE is empty or shows wrong-words (says 'cat' for 'dog'). Difficulty with vocabulary, sentence structure. CHILD 2 — SPEECH SOUND DISORDER: child says 'wabbit' for 'rabbit', 'fum' for 'thumb' — speech bubble shows the WORDS WITH WRONG SOUNDS articulated. The speech therapist holds a small mirror in front of the child's mouth to show tongue position. CHILD 3 — STUTTERING (Childhood-Onset Fluency Disorder): child says 'M-m-m-mommy I w-w-w-want' — speech bubble is BROKEN/FRAGMENTED with the same syllable repeated. A frustration expression on face. The therapist demonstrates a hand-tapping rhythm technique. CHILD 4 — SOCIAL (PRAGMATIC) COMMUNICATION DISORDER: child at a school table NOT taking turns in conversation, interrupting, missing nonverbal cues from peers. A poster of social rules on the wall ('TAKE TURNS', 'EYE CONTACT', 'WAIT YOUR TURN') with red X-marks where the child has missed. CRITICAL: this child has normal grammar/vocabulary but fails at SOCIAL USE.
